summary: Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1937–1938). He served as Director General of Archæology at the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968) and was a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1968–1971).
Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied under Olivier Lacombe, Michel Hulin, and completed doctoral studies under T. R. V. Murti.

Amanda K. Goodman is a specialist in Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, supervised by Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.
Amar Nath Pandeya is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Delhi (attested 1968) and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (attested 1987).

Amar Singh works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He studied under Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963) and under doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder (attested 1984), alongside teachers Bimal Krishna Matilal, T. Venkatacharya, Shoryu Katsura, M. Fujimoto, and Alasdair Urquhart.

Amara Ali is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. In 2026, she is attested as a Lecturer in Urdu at both the University of California, Berkeley and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Amaranatha Jha studied at Colonelganj Inter College and Muir Central College (BA ~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).
Amarasvar Thakur was an Indology scholar who held a post at the University of Calcutta (attested 1936) and served as General Editor of the Calcutta Sanskrit Series.

Amartya Sen works in philosophy and other fields. Educated at the University of Calcutta (~1951–1953) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1953–1959), he taught at Jadavpur, Delhi, and the LSE, and became a professor of economics and philosophy at Harvard University (~1987).
Amaury de Riencourt was a scholar in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed his education at the University of Algiers (MA), the Sorbonne, and the University of Paris.
Amba Kulkarni is a scholar of computational linguistics and Indology. She earned her PhD at the University of Hyderabad by 2009, where she later served as Professor (attested 2018–2026).

Amber D. Carpenter is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under M. M. McCabe, Verity Harte, and others. She has held posts at the University of St Andrews, University of York, Einstein Forum (2008), and Yale-NUS College.

Ambrogio Ballini was an Indologist who studied at Bologna, Bonn, Padua, and Milan under Carlo Formichi and Hermann Jacobi, among others. He was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Padua (1913), Università Cattolica (1924), and Sapienza University of Rome (1941–1949).

Amelia Bonea is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (BA) and Heidelberg University (PhD 2008–2012). She held posts at Oxford (2012–2017) and Heidelberg (2018–2022) before joining the University of Manchester (~2021).

Amelia Hall is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who received her doctorate from the University of Oxford in 2012. In 2019, she held posts at Naropa University as Assistant Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism and at Central Michigan University.
Ameneh Shirazinejad is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held posts as an Arabic language tutor at George Washington University and as a Visiting Fellow at the University of Delhi.

Amin Sweeney was a linguistics scholar who completed his doctorate at the University of London (~1967–1970). He held posts at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977) and UC Berkeley, where he chaired South and Southeast Asian Studies (1986–1991).
Amita Chatterjee is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University (attested 1999 and 2009).
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amrit Madhav Ghatage was an Indologist and linguist. He was Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1961–1978) and later served as Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1993–2003).
